sampling_model.design: Independent and identically distributed observational or fixed-randomization sampling from \(P\); the known benchmark \(b_a\) is conceptually distinct from the observational propensity \(e_a\).
sampling_model.treatment: A fixed finite action set \(\mathcal A=\{0,\ldots,J-1\}\) under consistency, conditional exchangeability, and uniform overlap.
sampling_model.overlap: \(e_a(X)\ge\epsilon\) and \(b_a(X)\ge\epsilon_b\) almost surely for every action, with \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}b_a(X)=1\) almost surely.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A fixed number of balanced folds is used. Conditional on each training complement, clipped outcome and propensity learners have uniform \(L^2(P_X)\) errors of orders \(r_{m,n}\) and \(r_{e,n}\); orthogonality makes the conditional score bias order \(r_{m,n}r_{e,n}\), and \(\sqrt n r_{m,n}r_{e,n}\to0\). Fold conclusions are combined by a fixed-fold union bound, not by asserting independence of overlapping training complements.

Orthogonal function-valued Z-estimators admit uniform Bahadur representations and simultaneous estimated-score multiplier confidence bands under high-level approximation and entropy conditions.
Neyman orthogonality and cross-fitting deliver root-\(n\) inference for regular low-dimensional targets under nuisance product-rate conditions.
Gaussian and multiplier couplings approximate suprema of empirical processes under complexity and moment bounds.
A nonzero second derivative under first-order degeneracy yields a second-order limit and generally invalidates the standard bootstrap.

body.tldr: On the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass of FangRidderXie2026, with \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), every maintained optimizer path is either identically the benchmark rule or has a divergence derivative uniformly bounded away from zero on \(\mathcal C\). The established joint uniform influence law and shared conditional multiplier process yield a simultaneous welfare--divergence tube indexed by penalty and valid after any measurable selection of the displayed penalty. Eventwise set-valued inversion reports all welfare values compatible with a selected divergence without requiring a derivative or branch choice; it remains the safe construction for the constant path or any nonregular extension. The Hessian quadratic form separately calibrates the \(n\)-scaled penalized-regret process.

project_justification.gap: FangRidderXie2026 proves efficiency and regret limits at a fixed positive preference and illustrates a three-arm commitment-savings frontier, but does not provide a simultaneous welfare--divergence tube after inspecting a preference path. Generic indexed-inference results do not establish the fold-specific learned-influence replacement along the same-sample implicit optimizer path, and they do not provide the softmax-specific constant-versus-uniformly-monotone divergence dichotomy.
project_justification.niche: On the common finite-action exponential-tilt subclass, feature identification, uniform interiority, smoothness, and curvature imply the exact identities \(H_c\theta_c'=-g_c\), \(dK(\theta_c)/dc=-g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c\), and \(dW(\theta_c)/dc=c\,dK(\theta_c)/dc\). If the optimizer equals the benchmark parameter at one penalty, the path equation forces equality everywhere; otherwise feature identification makes the divergence derivative strictly negative everywhere, and continuity on compact \(\mathcal C\) gives a uniform slope floor.
project_justification.fill: The note proves a joint uniform influence expansion for the optimizer, welfare, divergence, and implemented-rule evaluation paths, consistently estimates their covariance kernel, and validates one shared conditional multiplier process. The resulting penalty-indexed tube remains valid after measurable inspection-based selection. For divergence reporting, eventwise set inversion retains every compatible preference and welfare value, including under a constant path or a relaxed nonregular model. The foldwise product-bias, shrinking empirical \(L^2\) envelope, global argmax localization, totalized Hessian, covariance replacement, and conditional chaining arguments make the band implementable.

body.related_work: FangRidderXie2026 supplies the broader admissible-rule framework and its three-arm commitment-savings frontier. Its Theorems 1, 2, and 5 give fixed-positive-penalty efficiency, quadratic regret, and efficient doubly robust optimizer limits. This note does not claim their general continuous- or mixed-treatment classes: it works on the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered exponential-tilt/softmax subclass, where the faithful coordinate map is \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The advances established in the present graph are uniform path inference, selection-valid simultaneous reporting, uniform penalized-regret calibration, and a softmax-specific uniform divergence-slope result. BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 supplies a generic estimated-score multiplier architecture, while this note verifies its foldwise same-sample-path replacement inputs. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML supplies the cross-fitting and product-rate architecture, ChenFang2019 motivates second-order calibration under first-order degeneracy, and eventwise set inversion follows the logic of RenTelschowSchwartzman2024.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The maintained nonconstant softmax model has neither a population tangency nor a self-intersection because its divergence derivative is uniformly negative. Nevertheless, the current formal confidence construction is the penalty-indexed simultaneous tube together with eventwise set-valued inversion; no separate smooth sample-inverse Bahadur theorem or fixed-divergence plug-in welfare band is asserted here. Set-valued inversion is needed for the constant path, for finite-sample diagnostics that do not certify regular inversion, or after relaxing the identification and curvature conditions. Conditional multiplier validity requires the declared fixed dimension, bounded outcomes and features, overlap, fixed folds, nuisance consistency, product rate, global uniqueness, uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, and positive curvature floor. The totalized Hessian is essential off the high-probability regular event. The results exclude vanishing penalties, weak overlap, growing dimension, adaptive sampling, nonunique optimizers, and claims of optimal tube width; penalized-regret calibration is not an unpenalized-welfare regret theorem.
body.honest_scope: The contribution is estimation and inference for a causal welfare--divergence frontier on a fixed finite-dimensional, finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass; identification is taken as given. The established inference headline is the uniform penalty-indexed influence law and its post-selection-valid shared-multiplier tube. The strengthened geometry proves that a nonconstant maintained path has a uniformly regular population divergence coordinate, while set-valued inversion is the formally supported divergence-reporting method and also covers the constant or nonregular fallback. FangRidderXie2026 covers a broader admissible-rule setting; only the common softmax subclass is compared, using \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). No smooth estimated-inverse expansion is claimed in the present graph, and no result is asserted for continuous or mixed treatments, \(c\to0\), weak overlap, growing features, nonunique optima, adaptive samples, or minimax-optimal tube width.
body.interpretation: A planner may inspect the entire penalty-indexed welfare--divergence plot and then choose any measurable penalty while retaining the simultaneous tube guarantee. On a nonconstant maintained softmax path, divergence is a one-to-one population coordinate with slope uniformly separated from zero; on the constant path, every penalty gives the benchmark frontier point. The formally delivered divergence-reporting operation is set-valued inversion of the simultaneous tube: for a selected divergence it retains every compatible preference and all corresponding welfare values, so it also remains valid if an application relaxes the assumptions and permits tangencies or multiple branches. The identity \(a_c=cg_c\) explains cancellation of optimizer influence in the penalized welfare contrast, while the separate quadratic process measures penalized-welfare loss at the fitted rule on the natural \(n^{-1}\) scale.
